items.briefing:
South Australia has launched a Royal Commission into artificial intelligence, signalling growing government scrutiny of AI use across the country — something that may affect how training organisations adopt AI tools. Separately, experts are urging Australia to consider banning smart glasses capable of covert filming, raising real privacy concerns for staff and students in shared learning environments.

On a positive note, an Australian startup called Quantum Lock is developing new technology to detect cyberattacks on embedded devices using quantum physics, showing local innovation in the security space.

**Practical tip:** Remind staff that recording others without consent — including via wearable devices — may breach privacy laws and your organisation's own policies.

featured.title: South Australia launches Royal Commission into artificial intelligence
featured.quote: South Australia's Royal Commission on AI will shape critical governance for emerging technology risks.
